label: early original-phase steps (t=1-2) after a w/k/l prefix or on input w
explanation: Active almost only in the original phase at steps t=1-3 (98.8% of mass; t=2 alone holds 64%, t=1 28%). It never fires at t=0, almost never in the copy phase, and rarely on <DEL> (1.2% of mass). Within those early steps it is token-driven: it fires most when w, k or l appeared earlier (prev_tok w gives 9.6x lift, k 6.4x, l 4.5x; first_tok w 6.2x) or when the current input is w (5.6x). The strongest activations are prefixes like "w w", "k w w", "l w w" at t=2. Activation is higher on first occurrences of a token and lower in digit-heavy sequences. The predicate captures 82% of mass on dev but precision is only about 0.26, because many early steps after w/k/l stay inactive. Firing looks like a graded mix of early-prefix token identities rather than one crisp condition.
